excerpt: With Amazon IVS, you can stream without needing to manage or develop components on your own.
Describes in detail the IVS data-plane API for broadcast-software developers implementing client support for multitrack video.
Integrate into interactive apps with chat APIs, and Player and Broadcast SDKs for mobile and web.
Use the same live streaming technology and global infrastructure that powers Twitch.
Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) offers pay-as-you-go pricing.
When enabled, you send multiple video quality versions directly from your device and are charged a lower price as Amazon IVS does not need to generate these versions.

When broadcasting the stage to a channel, you have the option of client-side composition at no extra cost or [server-side composition](#Server-side_Composition) which incurs an additional hourly rate.
Deliver live streams with a latency that can be under 300 milliseconds from host to viewer.
Accommodate audiences beyond 25,000 viewers and enable up to 12 hosts to take the virtual stage.
By integrating the Amazon IVS broadcast SDKs for Android and iOS, your users can engage as hosts or viewers, enjoying high-quality live streams on their mobile devices.
Guest spots — Create applications that allow hosts to promote guests "on stage," turning viewers into hosts for real-time interactions.
Audio rooms — Invite listeners to join the conversation as guests and foster deeper engagement in your audio rooms.
When you stream, Amazon IVS automatically ingests video at a location near you.
Appending `--region <aws-region>` to your CLI command.
You can use Amazon EventBridge to monitor your Amazon Interactive Video Service (IVS) streams.
You can create a rule that triggers on an event emitted by Amazon IVS.
A publisher has connected to the stage and is being recorded to S3.
Get instant feedback from viewers of low-latency streams with polling and voting applications that use timed metadata.
Synchronize companion retail elements with low-latency streams or run live auctions with real-time streams.
Let your audiences interact by adding a virtual space to chats alongside your live content.

Commenter found IVS pricing "pretty good, surprisingly" and 2-second latency "not bad," noting it takes RTMP in and outputs m3u8. But their math for a large Twitch-scale streamer (~20k concurrent viewers, 10 hours from NA) came to about $20 input plus $30k output, a worst case of ~$30,020/day, which they called "still financially unviable" at that scale.

Commenter compared IVS's timed-metadata feature (firing in-app events such as a 'buy now' button synced to the live stream) to a contextual-merchandising system they built about 20 years ago alongside WWE live streams. They called IVS a "pretty cool" descendant of that idea.
